title: Continuity proxy for graceful region handoff and stream-preserving failover
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a lightweight continuity proxy component at the edge that enables graceful multi-region handoff for long-lived streaming sessions and request sessions. The proxy preserves live streams, avoids user-visible truncation, and enforces region-aware circuit-breaking and prioritized shed rules so we meet customer-facing SLOs during regional degradations.
background: Recent incidents showed that large-region outages cause abrupt stream termination and request loss for hosted API customers. Existing failover mechanisms reroute traffic but drop in-flight streaming sessions or force immediate client reconnects. For low-latency chat and assistant integrations this manifests as truncated responses or duplicate partial replies and increases error budgets. We need a mechanism to preserve session continuity during an upstream region switchover while still protecting backbone capacity with clear circuit-breaker boundaries.
goals: Preserve in-flight streaming sessions across region handoff with <= 99.5% probability of no visible truncation for sessions < 10 minutes
Ensure 99th percentile request latency SLOs are not violated by > 5% of incidents during reconfiguration windows
Provide deterministic load-shedding policy that prioritizes authenticated, paid customers and control-plane traffic
Expose observability (per-session handoff counts, buffer-drain durations, shed events) and runbook hooks for on-call teams
non_goals: Full stateful session migration for arbitrarily large KV caches (out of scope)
Replacing existing long-term session persistence mechanisms in Dedicated/Private
design_summary: Introduce 'continuity-proxy' as a small, stateless edge shim with three modes: proxy-pass, buffer-drain, and replay-redirect. The proxy keeps an ephemeral per-session buffer (bounded by size/time), mirrors minimal session metadata to a light-weight shared control plane (region-aware index), and coordinates handoff using a two-phase signal: START_DRAIN and COMPLETE_HANDOFF. During START_DRAIN the proxy allows existing upstream connections to finish while rejecting new heavy requests, applying circuit-breaker thresholds to upstream region. If upstream fails to complete within drain window, the proxy switches to replay-redirect to a compatible region variant and emits explicit session markers so clients and SDKs can deduplicate partial outputs.
acceptance_criteria: E2E test where primary region is killed and continuity-proxy drains active 5-minute streams without observable truncation in 95% of runs
Dashboard shows per-region handoff rate, average drain time, and shed-rate by customer tier
Post-deploy chaos run (region outage) does not increase API 99th percentile latency by more than 5% for tiered customers after proxy rollout
Runbook documents steps to force immediate failover, extend drain window, and disable proxy per-region
tasks: Spec: define protocol between edge gateway and continuity-proxy (control signals and telemetry schema)
Prototype: implement Go-based proxy with buffered streaming wire protocol support
Circuit breaker policy: add region-level token-bucket and per-customer priority lanes
Integration: wire proxy into existing gateway chain (pre-auth stage) and ensure compatibility with streaming SDKs
Tests: unit tests, integration tests in staging (chaos injection), benchmark harness for drain-window sizing
Observability: dashboards, logs, per-session traces, SLO alerting rules
Runbook: on-call steps, rollback plan, and customer communication template
implementation_notes: Use bounded in-memory ring buffer per session (default 1MB or 30s worth of tokens) to avoid unbounded memory growth
Expose a 'session.serial' marker token appended to stream events to enable client deduplication on replay
Reuse existing KV index for minimal session metadata but do not replicate full KV cache; store only: session_id, created_at, primary_region, last_event_seq
Circuit breaker levels: warning at 70% capacity, shed-low-priority at 85%, hard-cut at 95%
Default drain window 12s (tunable per-tenant), parameterized via route config
Ensure TLS termination and mutual auth are preserved; continuity-proxy runs in same tenant VPC to preserve compliance constraints
tradeoffs: Buffered approach avoids immediate truncation but increases memory pressure at edge; mitigated by strict per-session caps and eviction policies
Two-phase handoff adds latency for failover completion but preserves user-visible continuity; acceptable for interactive chat but may not suit streaming telemetry consumers
Keeping proxy stateless with minimal shared index reduces complexity but limits ability to migrate huge session caches
testing_plan: Unit: buffer edge cases (overflow, partial writes), marker token correctness
Integration: simulate region flaps in staging; assert client-visible continuity metrics
Performance: long-run soak with 10k concurrent streams to validate memory bounds and circuit-breaker thresholds
Chaos: kill primary region components and measure drain success rate and SLO delta
Security: run internal pentest on proxy ingress path and validate KMS interactions
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Canary: deploy to us-west-2 edge only for internal dev orgs (1 week)
Phase 1 - Beta: enable for 10% external traffic with feature flag and monitor SLOs (2 weeks)
Phase 2 - Ramp: 50% traffic across 3 low-risk regions with automated rollback on SLO breach
Phase 3 - Global: full roll, enable per-tenant tuning UI in Console
runbook_snippet: If handoff fail rate > 2% for 10m: increase drain_window to 30s for affected region and notify on-call
If memory pressure on edge node > 80%: flip feature flag to reject new proxy buffers and fallback to immediate redirect
To force immediate failover: set COMPLETE_HANDOFF timeout to 0 and enable replay-redirect for the route
